segments.text: Welcome to your daily robotics digest from August 25th, 2026.
Today we cover NEC's investment, humanoid robot competition results, and automated delivery systems.
Stay informed with us.
From Robotics & Automation News, NEC invests in US-based robotics startup Dexmate.
This report details an investment by NEC's corporate venture capital fund into Dexmate, a robotics startup developing the VEGA humanoid robot and an integrated physical AI development platform.

The company's methodology focuses on simplifying the deployment of physical artificial intelligence by combining sensors, control systems, and simulation environments to streamline the development and deployment of physical AI systems across diverse industries.

NEC intends to integrate Dexmate's technology with its existing artificial intelligence expertise to explore applications within the field of Physical AI, supporting NEC's open innovation strategy for new business development.
This move indicates a strategic alignment between large technology corporations and specialized hardware-software solutions in the physical AI domain.
From Humanoids Daily, "Robots Outrun Usain Bolt: Inside the Record-Shattering Spree at the 2nd World Humanoid Robot Games".
This report details how Chinese humanoid robots achieved track-and-field record times at the recent World Humanoid Robot Games.
Chinese humanoid robots, including models such as the Tiangong Ultra, accomplished sub-ten-second 100m sprints and sub-forty-second 400m runs, exceeding the benchmarks set by Usain Bolt.
Furthermore, these robotic systems established new marks in the 1500m run and standing high jump during the competition.
However, the robots encountered difficulties with deceleration and directional stability, leading to several incidents of physical impact.
Experts indicate a necessary pivot in research focus toward developing practical environmental navigation capabilities.
This development signals a shift in focus within the AI and robotics industry toward real-world application challenges.
From Robotics & Automation News, J&T Express adds twenty-two automated sorting systems as unmanned delivery fleet tops one thousand nine hundred.
This report details an expansion of automation within the logistics sector, reflecting significant technological integration in delivery operations.
J&T Global Express has integrated twenty-two new automated sorting systems, bringing the total count across its network to four hundred thirty-five.
This expansion coincides with an eight-seventy percent increase in unmanned delivery vehicles, which now exceed one thousand nine hundred units as of the end of June two thousand twenty-six.

The company is pursuing efficiency and cost reduction through outlet automation and the deployment of intelligent systems, with the new sorting equipment being established across Southeast Asia, China, and other markets.
Furthermore, J&T is concentrating efforts on employing artificial intelligence for quality inspection and intelligent route planning within its logistics framework.
This development indicates a growing trend toward fully autonomous logistics solutions driven by advanced artificial intelligence.
From Humanoids Daily, Figure AI Demonstrates 15-Foot Autonomous Ladder Ascent and Descent for Industrial Mezzanines.
This report details the autonomous climbing and descending of a fifteen-foot industrial ladder achieved by the Figure AI system utilizing its Helix software architecture.
The task required continuous coordination of visual perception, dynamic balance, and contact loading across the entire body to navigate the ascent and descent.
This accomplishment involved tightly coupling perception, planning, and dynamic control in a continuous manner to manage the complex physical requirements of the task.
This capability is essential for humanoid robots seeking general-purpose labor utility in complex, unstructured workspaces.
The successful demonstration signals significant progress toward realizing practical, complex mobility for humanoid robotics applications.
From Humanoids Daily, AdaPT Bridges Sim-to-Real to Teach Humanoids the Tennis Styles of Federer, Nadal, and Djokovic.
This report details a framework that transfers complex tennis playing styles from video to humanoid robots.
The system employs a decoupled planning-and-tracking hierarchy augmented with explicit speed adaptation to mitigate simulation to reality discrepancies and real-world latency.
Training data was derived by mining three-dimensional body meshes from broadcast video to capture intricate biomechanics, including topspin follow-through.
Testing on robots such as the Unitree G1 and Dobot Atom demonstrated marked improvements in hit rates and serve success when compared against non-adaptive methodologies.
AdaPT establishes a pathway for transferring advanced athletic skills from visual information into physical humanoid systems in practical environments.
This advancement indicates a viable method for complex skill acquisition in robotics.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Regular Price ROSCon Tickets Extended until August 27th".
This report details an extension of sales for regular price ROSCon tickets, facilitated by support from Destination Toronto.
Ticket sales are now open until Friday, August 28th, 2026, at 6:59 AM UTC, granting additional time for ticket purchases.
This extension was implemented to accommodate increased demand for event attendance.
The extension was made possible through collaboration with Destination Toronto, which provided the necessary support to facilitate the extended sales window.
This measure allows interested parties more time to secure entry to the conference.
The decision reflects an effort to maximize accessibility to the event.
Attention should be directed toward further updates regarding conference attendance logistics.
From Robotics & Automation News, "How to Select Roller Brushes for Robotic Solar Panel Cleaning Systems".

This report examines the criteria for selecting roller brushes in robotic solar panel cleaning systems, concluding that the choice depends on site contamination, cleaning method, and robot interface rather than solely brush softness.
The methodology detailed the necessity of balancing cleaning action with controlled contact, serviceability, and module limitations.
Findings indicate that loose dust necessitates soft brushing techniques, whereas hard deposits such as bird droppings require more nuanced approaches.
The selection process must account for module cleaning guidance and surface protection, integrating brush condition and operating conditions into the overall system assessment.
A suitable roller controls routine soiling while recognizing when alternative cleaning methods are required.
This development indicates an increased focus on systems-level integration in the robotics and automation sector moving forward.
From Humanoids Daily, Pink Robotics Emerges in Germany With a Mission to Revive Industrial Engineering.
This report details the introduction of a new humanoid robot designed for logistics sorting.
Pink Robotics, a company based in Darmstadt, has unveiled the P0, a 1.75-meter-tall humanoid robot.
This machine features thirty-two degrees of freedom, weighs eighty-two kilograms, and possesses an eight kilogram payload capacity.
The company intends to utilize this technology to revitalize the German industrial sector.
Pink Robotics is currently organizing a logistics pilot program with a major supermarket chain to assess the robot's operational capabilities.
The startup is simultaneously seeking seed funding to establish a competitive position against other entities in the humanoid robotics field.
This development signals continued investment in practical industrial applications for advanced robotics systems.
From MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech, "I spent a day at a robot “carnival” in Shanghai. Here’s what I saw."
This report details the progress of embodied artificial intelligence through humanoid robotics development in China.
Humanoid robots are a focus in China's strategy to integrate artificial intelligence into daily life, with the country accounting for nearly ninety percent of those delivered worldwide last year.
A robot carnival in Shanghai demonstrated various robotic capabilities, including tasks such as making coffee and engaging public displays.
These events serve to popularize robotics and address prior safety concerns related to humanoids through public exposure.
Chinese firms are actively advancing these developments, successfully attracting public interest in the field.
This trend signals a significant acceleration in the deployment of embodied AI systems across various sectors.
And that's all the circuits we have for today!
Hope your day runs smoothly, much like Dexmate's latest investment.
Until tomorrow, keep those algorithms humming!
Bye for now.
